q: To save her baby boy from Pharaoh, what did Moses' mother put him in?
why: She coated it with tar and pitch so it would float.
quote: she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch.

q: Where did Moses' mother place the basket with her baby inside?
a: Among the reeds by the Nile
why: She hid him along the riverbank.
quote: set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.

q: Who stood at a distance to watch what would happen to baby Moses in the basket?
why: She kept watch over her little brother.
quote: And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.

q: Who found baby Moses in his basket by the Nile?
why: She came down to the river to bathe.
quote: Soon the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the Nile

q: Why did Pharaoh's daughter name the baby from the basket Moses?
a: She drew him out of the water
wrong: He was born on the Nile
why: Moses became her son.
quote: She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.”

q: While Moses was tending sheep at Horeb, what amazing sight did he see?
a: A burning bush not burning up
why: The angel of the LORD appeared in the fire.
quote: Moses saw the bush ablaze with fire, but it was not consumed.

q: At the burning bush, what did God tell Moses to take off?
why: Moses was standing on holy ground.
quote: Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.

q: At the burning bush, to whom did God send Moses?
why: Moses was to bring God's people out of Egypt.
quote: I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.

q: When Moses asked God's name at the burning bush, what did God answer?
why: Moses was to tell Israel that I AM had sent him.
quote: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.

q: In the first plague on Egypt, what did the water of the Nile turn into?
why: Aaron struck the river with his staff.
quote: and all the water was turned to blood.

q: During the plagues on Egypt, God warned Pharaoh He would fill the country with which animal?
why: Pharaoh still refused to let the people go.
quote: I will plague your whole country with frogs.

q: During the plagues on Egypt, what fell from the sky with thunder and lightning?
why: Moses stretched his staff toward heaven.
quote: So the LORD rained down hail upon the land of Egypt.

q: During the plagues on Egypt, which insects did God bring after the hail?
why: They covered the land and ate what was left.
quote: I will bring locusts into your territory tomorrow.

q: During the plagues on Egypt, how long did total darkness cover the land?
why: No one in Egypt could see anyone else.
quote: and total darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days.

q: Before the plagues began, what message from the LORD did Moses and Aaron bring Pharaoh?
why: God wanted His people to worship Him in the wilderness.
quote: Let My people go

q: When Moses first asked Pharaoh to free Israel, how did Pharaoh answer?
a: I will not let Israel go
why: Pharaoh said he did not know the LORD.
quote: and I will not let Israel go.

q: In front of Pharaoh, what did Aaron's staff do to the magicians' staffs?
why: God showed He was greater than Egypt's magic.
quote: But Aaron’s staff swallowed up the other staffs.

q: For the first Passover, what animal was each family to choose?
why: One lamb was chosen for each household.
quote: each man must select a lamb for his family, one per household.

q: For the first Passover, what kind of lamb was needed?
why: The lamb had to be perfect.
quote: Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male

q: At the first Passover, where did the Israelites put the lamb's blood?
why: The blood marked the houses of God's people.
quote: They are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes

q: At the first Passover, what did the Israelites eat with the roasted lamb?
why: They ate the meal that same night.
quote: along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

q: At the first Passover, what did God do when He saw the blood on a house?
why: That is why the feast is called the Passover.
quote: when I see the blood, I will pass over you.

q: At midnight on the first Passover, what happened in Egypt?
why: It was the last of the ten plagues.
quote: Now at midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn male in the land of Egypt

q: After the tenth plague, what did Pharaoh tell Moses and the Israelites?
why: Pharaoh finally let God's people go.
quote: Get up, leave my people, both you and the Israelites!

q: As the Israelites left Egypt, what went before them to guide them by day?
why: By night a pillar of fire gave them light.
quote: And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day

q: When Pharaoh's army chased Israel to the edge of the sea, how did the Israelites feel?
why: They cried out to the LORD.
quote: and they were terrified and cried out to the LORD.

q: At the sea, Moses said the LORD would fight for Israel. What did the people need to do?
why: God Himself would save them.
quote: The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still.

q: At the sea, what did God tell Moses to lift up and stretch out over the water?
why: God would divide the sea.
quote: lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it

q: When Israel was trapped by the sea, what did the LORD use to drive back the water all night?
why: The wind turned the sea into dry land.
quote: the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind that turned it into dry land.

q: When God divided the sea, how did the Israelites cross?
why: Walls of water stood on both sides.
quote: and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground

q: What happened to Pharaoh's army when it followed Israel into the sea?
why: Not one of them survived.
quote: The waters flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen

q: After Israel crossed the sea, who led the women with tambourines and dancing?
why: Miriam was Aaron's sister and a prophetess.
quote: Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took a tambourine in her hand

q: In the wilderness after leaving Egypt, what did the hungry Israelites complain about?
why: They remembered the food of Egypt.
quote: but you have brought us into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death!

q: When Israel was hungry in the wilderness, what did God promise to rain down from heaven?
why: The people were to gather enough each day.
quote: Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you.

q: That evening in the wilderness, what birds came and covered Israel's camp?
why: God gave them meat in the evening.
quote: That evening quail came and covered the camp

q: When the Israelites first saw thin flakes on the desert floor, what did they ask?
why: Moses told them it was bread from the LORD.
quote: they asked one another, “What is it?”

q: What did the Israelites call the bread God gave them in the wilderness?
why: They ate it every day in the wilderness.
quote: Now the house of Israel called the bread manna.

q: What did the manna in the wilderness taste like?
why: God's bread was sweet.
quote: and tasted like wafers made with honey.

q: For how many years did the Israelites eat manna?
why: They ate it until they reached Canaan.
quote: The Israelites ate manna forty years

q: Which commandment comes first in the Ten Commandments?
why: God comes first.
quote: You shall have no other gods before Me.

q: In the Ten Commandments, which day were God's people told to keep holy?
why: It was a day of rest for the LORD.
quote: Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.

q: Which of the Ten Commandments comes with a promise of long life in the land?
why: God promised long days to those who honor their parents.
quote: Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land

q: Which of the Ten Commandments says not to take what belongs to others?
why: God's people respect what belongs to others.
quote: You shall not steal.

q: In the Ten Commandments, what must you not bear against your neighbor?
why: God's people must not lie about others.
quote: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

q: When God came down to give His law, what covered Mount Sinai?
why: The LORD came down on the mountain in fire.
quote: Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke

q: What were the tablets God gave Moses on Mount Sinai made of?
why: They held the words of God's covenant.
quote: tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God.

q: Who wrote on the stone tablets God gave Moses?
why: God Himself wrote His law.
quote: inscribed by the finger of God.

q: While Moses stayed long on Mount Sinai, what did the people ask Aaron to make?
why: They grew tired of waiting for Moses.
quote: Come, make us gods who will go before us.

q: At Mount Sinai, what did Aaron tell the people to bring him to make an idol?
why: He melted the gold to make the idol.
quote: Take off the gold earrings

q: What did Aaron make from the people's gold at Mount Sinai?
why: The people said the calf had brought them out of Egypt.
quote: he fashioned it into a molten calf.

q: When Moses came down and saw the golden calf, what did he do with the stone tablets?
why: Moses burned with anger at the people's sin.
quote: he burned with anger and threw the tablets out of his hands, shattering them

q: What did Moses do to the golden calf?
a: Burned it and ground it to powder
why: He destroyed the idol completely.
quote: burned it in the fire, ground it to powder

q: After the golden calf, Moses said, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me.” Who came?
why: The Levites stood with the LORD.
quote: And all the Levites gathered around him.

q: Why did the people at Mount Sinai ask Aaron to make them gods?
a: Moses was delayed on the mountain
why: They did not know what had happened to Moses.
quote: Now when the people saw that Moses was delayed in coming down from the mountain

q: At the start of Exodus, what was different about the new king who came to power in Egypt?
why: He feared the Israelites and made them slaves.
quote: Then a new king, who did not know Joseph, came to power in Egypt.

q: Which store cities did the enslaved Israelites build for Pharaoh?
why: Taskmasters forced them into hard labor.
quote: they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.

q: Why did the Hebrew midwives refuse Pharaoh's order to kill the baby boys?
why: They let the boys live.
quote: The midwives, however, feared God

q: Whom did Pharaoh's daughter pay to nurse baby Moses?
why: Moses' sister cleverly brought their mother.
quote: Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages.

q: After Moses killed an Egyptian, where did he flee to escape Pharaoh?
why: There he sat down beside a well.
quote: But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian

q: In Midian, whom did Moses marry?
why: She was the daughter of the priest of Midian.
quote: and he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage.

q: Whose flock was Moses tending when he saw the burning bush?
why: Jethro was the priest of Midian.
quote: Moses was shepherding the flock of his father-in-law Jethro

q: At the burning bush, how did God describe the land He would give Israel?
why: It was a good and spacious land.
quote: a land flowing with milk and honey

q: At the burning bush, what did Moses' staff become when he threw it down?
why: It was a sign so the people would believe Moses.
quote: and it became a snake, and he ran from it.

q: At the burning bush, why did Moses say he could not speak to Pharaoh?
why: God promised to teach him what to say.
quote: for I am slow of speech and tongue.

q: When Moses asked God to send someone else, whom did God send to speak for him?
why: Aaron could speak well.
quote: Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well

q: After Moses first spoke to Pharaoh, what did Pharaoh stop giving the Hebrew slaves?
why: Pharaoh made their work even harder.
quote: You shall no longer supply the people with straw for making bricks.

q: During the plagues on Egypt, what did the dust turn into when Aaron struck it?
why: Swarms of gnats covered the land.
quote: that it may turn into swarms of gnats throughout the land of Egypt.

q: During the plagues on Egypt, what broke out on people and animals from fine dust?
why: Even the magicians were struck with boils.
quote: and festering boils will break out on man and beast

q: What was the tenth and final plague on Egypt?
why: After it, Pharaoh let Israel go.
quote: and every firstborn son in the land of Egypt will die

q: After crossing the sea, why could the Israelites not drink the water at Marah?
why: Marah means bitter.
quote: they could not drink the water there because it was bitter.

q: At Marah, what did Moses throw into the bitter water to make it sweet?
why: The LORD showed him the log.
quote: And when he cast it into the waters, they were sweetened.

q: When Israel had no water at Horeb, what did God tell Moses to strike?
why: Water came out for the people to drink.
quote: And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.

q: In Israel's battle with Amalek, when did Israel win?
a: When Moses held up his hands
why: When Moses lowered his hands, Amalek won.
quote: As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed

q: In the battle with Amalek, who held up Moses' tired hands?
why: They held his hands steady until sunset.
quote: Then Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on each side

q: When Moses was worn out judging the people, what did Jethro advise him to do?
why: The work was too heavy for one man.
quote: Appoint them over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.

q: The Ten Commandments forbid making an idol in the form of what?
a: Anything in heaven, earth, or water
why: Nothing created should be worshiped.
quote: You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.

q: What reason do the Ten Commandments give for resting on the Sabbath?
a: God rested on the seventh day
why: God made everything in six days.
quote: but on the seventh day He rested.

q: How long did Moses stay on Mount Sinai inside the cloud?
why: God gave him instructions there.
quote: and he remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

q: How did the LORD speak with Moses at the tent of meeting?
a: Face to face, like a friend
why: Moses had a close friendship with God.
quote: Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.

q: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the new tablets, what was different about him?
why: He had been speaking with the LORD.
quote: he was unaware that his face had become radiant from speaking with the LORD.

q: When the tabernacle was finished, what filled it?
why: The cloud covered the Tent of Meeting.
quote: and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.

q: What were the names of the Hebrew midwives who disobeyed Pharaoh?
why: They feared God more than the king.
quote: whose names were Shiphrah and Puah

q: How long did Moses' mother hide him before putting him in a basket?
why: She saw he was a beautiful child.
quote: she hid him for three months.

q: What did Moses name the son Zipporah bore him in Midian?
why: Moses felt like a foreigner in a foreign land.
quote: and Moses named him Gershom

q: At which mountain did Moses see the burning bush?
why: He had led the flock to the far side of the wilderness.
quote: and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

q: About how many men on foot left Egypt with Moses?
why: Women and children came too.
quote: with about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children.

q: How long had the Israelites lived in Egypt before the exodus?
why: Then they left on the very same day.
quote: Now the duration of the Israelites’ stay in Egypt was 430 years.

q: From which city did the Israelites set out when they left Egypt?
why: Their first stop was Succoth.
quote: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth

q: Near which place did Pharaoh's army catch up with Israel camped by the sea?
why: It was opposite Baal-zephon.
quote: as they camped by the sea near Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon.

q: What did the manna in the wilderness look like?
why: It tasted like honey wafers.
quote: It was white like coriander seed

q: What kind of wood was the ark of the covenant made of?
why: God gave exact measurements for the ark.
quote: And they are to construct an ark of acacia wood

q: Who was Moses' young assistant who would not leave the tent of meeting?
why: Joshua later led Israel into Canaan.
quote: but his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.

q: During Moses' second forty days on Mount Sinai, what did he go without?
why: He wrote the Ten Commandments on the tablets.
quote: without eating bread or drinking water.

q: The Ten Commandments say God shows loving devotion to how many generations of those who love Him?
why: His love lasts far longer than punishment.
quote: but showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me
